findings_reconciliation.F1734_R01_coordinates_reconciliation: Verified that the actual Python audit script and finite element meshes have always operated in the correct benchmark coordinates (x in [0, 1] mm, y in [0, 1] mm). The trajectory evaluated is strictly (0.50, 0.50) mm to (0.65, 0.55) mm with length 158.11 um (21.08 l0). The '(30.0, 50.0) to (43.5, 59.0)' text in the previous report was a markdown transcription typo, not an execution or geometry defect.
findings_reconciliation.F1734_R02_sampling_specification_reconci: Both immutable meshes (F1732 and F1734) have now been re-evaluated using identical geometry, identical disjoint station intervals (s_min <= proj < s_max), identical transverse half-width (w_perp = 2.5 l0 = 18.75 um, total width 37.5 um), and identical area-equivalent h metric.

F1734_R03_continuity_and_coarse_gap_eval.assessment: In F1732, noncompliant elements form a continuous transverse barrier spanning across the entire corridor width (transverse span = 37.5 um, longitudinal span = 78.4 um = 10.45 l0), blocking crack propagation with coarse elements up to 7.8 um. In F1734, the largest coarse cluster spans only a fraction of the corridor and does NOT form a transverse barrier (has_transverse_coarse_barrier = False). Continuous process-zone resolution (h <= 3.75 um) exists throughout the primary fracture corridor.

F1734_R04_station7_clarification.clarification: Station 7 achieves mean h = 2.506 um, which strictly satisfies h <= l0/2 = 3.75 um (with 100.0% count and 100.0% area compliance). It does NOT strictly satisfy h <= l0/3 = 2.50 um since 2.506 > 2.50. The previous statement claiming Stations 1-7 satisfy h <= l0/3 is formally corrected to Stations 1-6.
